subject: Throughput & Economics: continuous-batching expectations + next steps (Olive Health)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@olivehealth.com>; Olive Health Technical Team <eng@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput & Economics: continuous-batching expectations + next steps (Olive Health)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can scope a clean POC and sizing estimate.

Key notes I captured from the call: 
- Expected steady-state monthly usage: ~45M tokens (chat-style interactions, avg prompt+response ~350 tokens).
- Peak 95th percentile concurrency: ~18–25 req/s, mostly small chat responses; bursty spikes to ~50 req/s for marketing events.
- Workload pattern: long-running product demos and scheduled background inference; customers expect near-continuous traffic rather than occasional batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: 300–500ms p95 for short responses; streaming preferred for UX.
- Target unit economics: Olive is aiming for ~$250–$350 per 1M tokens for a production deployment (team-level target).

Open clarifying questions for you (so we can finalize cost assumptions):
1) Can you confirm the split between short (<=200 token) vs long (>500 token) responses? A rough % is fine.
2) Any hard constraint on p95 latency for long responses?
3) Do you plan to use streaming for all user-facing responses, or only for >300 token outputs?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share the POC requirements doc from the call (attachments welcome), we'll sketch an architecture + continuous batching config and return a pricing estimate (inc. expected $/1M tokens) by EOD Friday.
- Technical sync with our runtime engineer (30–45m) to validate concurrency/batching assumptions.

Attaching a short template for required POC detail (happy to accept your existing doc).

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: poc_template.md (stub)

From: Alice Chen <alice@olivehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olive Health Technical Team <eng@olivehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T13:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & Economics: continuous-batching expectations + next steps (Olive Health)

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the recap. Quick answers and I've attached our PoC requirements PDF.

- Token split: ~70% short (<=200 tokens), 25% mid (200–600), 5% long (>600).
- Latency: for short responses p95 goal is 250–350ms; long responses can tolerate up to 1.2s p95 for streaming flows.
- Streaming: plan to stream for anything over ~250 tokens; single-shot for very short replies.
- Procurement: target budget band is $10k–$15k/mo to start (we're evaluating unit economics toward $250–$350 / 1M tokens).

Attached: olive_poc_requirements.pdf (POC scope + sample traffic traces).

We can do the technical sync next Wednesday — any time in the morning PT works.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Product | Olive Health
attachments: olive_poc_requirements.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>; Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & Economics: continuous-batching expectations + next steps (Olive Health)

Dylan / Sean — I reviewed Olive's POC doc and traffic traces. Draft pricing/assumptions below (for the external estimate). Please confirm before I export the Excel and send formally.

High-level assumptions (recommendation):
- Model: trimmed-medium open model (quantized 4-bit variant) — balances latency and quality for chat.
- Continuous batching mode: enabled with small max-latency window (20–30ms) to preserve p95 targets while allowing batching across streams. This is the primary lever to hit $/1M token targets.
- KV/prefix caching: enable for frequent prompts (estimated 12% token savings).
- Autoscale baseline: reserve capacity for 20 concurrent workers, burst policy to 50 for short windows.

Estimated unit economics (based on 45M monthly tokens):
- Baseline (with continuous batching + caching): ~$280 / 1M tokens (range $240–$320 depending on burst profile and quantization).
- Conservative (no batching / worst-case burst): ~$420 / 1M tokens.

Operational notes for POC:
- For the tech sync, bring traffic-replay traces and two canonical prompts to validate batching effectiveness.
- We'll instrument token-level cost breakdown and a live cost dashboard during the POC.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (contains detailed slab pricing, expected GPU hours, and the sensitivity table).

If folks are good with the $280 baseline, I can convert to a formal estimate and include an add-on line for a Dedicated pool if Olive wants a locked SLA.

- Marissa
Director, Revenue Engineering | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx

Alice — thanks for the doc and the timing commitment. Quick plan and proposed next steps: 

1) Formal estimate: Marissa provided a baseline of ~$280 / 1M tokens (range $240–$320). We'll draft a formal POC estimate (line items + sensitivity) and email it to you by COB tomorrow. Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (from Marissa).

2) Technical sync: propose Wed 08/26 10:00–10:45am PT. Agenda: validate replay traces, confirm streaming behavior, set batching window and concurrency knobs. Please confirm or suggest alternatives.

3) POC plan / timeline:
- Week 0: kick & infra provisioning (enable continuous-batching + KV cache).
- Week 1–2: smoke & replay tests, measure batching lift.
- Week 3–4: customer UAT + cost dashboard review.

4) Procurement: if Olive wants to hit the target $/1M tokens in the lower band (~$250), recommend a 3-month reserved capacity commit or a Dedicated pilot (we'll include both options). Can you loop in your procurement lead and an expected decision date?
